region_texts: ASIDE: An Agentic Self-Improving Data Engine
Industrial computer-vision projects are rarely bottlenecked by training YOLO or DETR;
they are bottlenecked by producing enough correctly labeled data. We present
(Agentic Self-Improving Data Engine), a research proposal and system architecture that
aims to reduce—not eliminate—human annotation cost for domain-specific object detec
tion. ASIDE combines public-dataset discovery, ontology alignment, schema normalization,
sequence-based annotation, retrieval-augmented visual memory, teacher-model consensus,
active learning, and downstream detector feedback into a closed loop.

region_texts: Version 0.1 does three things: (i) state the hypothesis mathematically; (ii) record the target
architecture and memory-binding formula; (iii) separate the scientific test order from claims
that cannot yet be made. This document is not an implementation guide or production API
specification; application frameworks, queues, and UI layers are deliberately out of scope.

Central hypothesis: from human annotation to a self-improving engine
The goal is not merely an auto-labeling script. It is to turn human labeling into a machine
assisted, self-correcting annotation process. Humans are not removed; cost is reduced. The
target regime is one in which humans touch only uncertain and novel examples.
This expands the project beyond a single detector into an agentic self-improving CV data
engine. The sequence annotator is one component of that engine, not the whole system.

region_texts: The target architecture runs from a user request to YOLO feedback. A Task Agent maps
the problem into an ontology. One branch discovers public datasets; another ingests customer
images. Both meet in a Schema Normalizer. A vision encoder produces embeddings; a Seq2Seq
annotator proposes labels; a VectorDB retrieves similar history; grounding, SAM 2, and an
existing YOLO (if any) provide second opinions. Consensus separates certain from uncertain
cases. Clean data trains YOLO; an Error Agent expands the dataset. Thick boxes in the
architecture are decision points; shaded paths are memory or uncertainty routes.
Task Agent and the agentic / deterministic split
Users should not supply technical dataset parameters. A sentence such as “I want to detect
holes, cracks, and abnormal veins in marble” becomes a structured problem: domain, material,
targets, tasks, optional attributes. An LLM may be used here. The design rule is explicit: we
will not make everything an agent.
format conversion, geometry, hashing, schema compile
Agents reason brittlely; conversion, normalization, and hashing must be reproducible code.
From Task Agent outputs (e.g., crack, hole, cavity, marble, industrial surface defect), a Dataset
Discovery Agent searches catalogs such as Kaggle and Hugging Face Hub. It does not search
only “marble”; it expands queries. Marble data may be scarce; granite / stone / surface-defect
data may still help transfer learning. Datasets are registered before training.
Registry fields include id, name, source, source_url, license, domain, image_count, annota
tion_format, resolution statistics, classes, quality_score, download_date, version, and option
ally a content hash. A License Agent separately checks commercial vs. research use.
A large dataset is not automatically better than a small one. A Quality Agent produces a
sample diversity. Weights are heuristic in v0.2 and may later be learned.
Dataset A may say “hole” and “crack”; Dataset B “cavity” and “fracture”; Dataset C “void” and
“fissure.” Blind merging creates spurious classes. An ontology maps source names to canonical
categories, each with a confidence. Low-confidence mappings go to human review—a “hole”
may be a surface void in one corpus and a drilled hole in another.

region_texts: Hard negatives and the self-improving loop
If the model confuses shadows with holes, naïve training asks for more holes. ASIDE asks
non-holes: shadows, dark veins, oil marks, reflections, dark discoloration—a hard
negative set that typically cuts industrial false positives.
The dataset is not a static file; it evolves from error signals. Hence
Kaggle images may have perfect lighting and fixed cameras; factories have sunlight, dust, water,
motion blur, and different materials. Public vs. factory embedding distributions are compared
(MMD, Fréchet, or centroid cosine—chosen in v0.3). Large distance means public data is
becomes the valuable asset; public catalogs are a ladder, not a permanent dependency.
Rich outputs, relations, and the role of YOLO
Sequence outputs need not stop at boxes. Future tokens may include severity, length, orien
tation, relations, and status. YOLO remains strong on class+geometry; the sequence layer
can carry attributes, relationships, context, and history. Example relations after detection:

At this level of definition, ASIDE is no longer “a Seq2Seq project that eases YOLO labeling.”
It is an autonomous CV data-production system that combines a Seq2Seq annotator, short
term temporal memory, VectorDB long-term visual memory, active learning, and downstream
detector feedback. In narrative form for v1.0 (not the v0.1 scope): the customer states a natural
language factory goal; the system builds an ontology, finds public data, scores quality, normalizes
schemas, trains a sequence annotator, encodes unlabeled images, binds similar history and
temporal memory, proposes labels, verifies with teachers, auto-accepts high reliability, routes
uncertainty to humans, writes corrections into error memory, trains YOLO, observes production
